arms.better: tm reached the relevant Path implementation and typing tests, but repeatedly reported reads of the same large src/click/types.py without showing what each read added, and stats recorded 775067 input tokens. It gave no visible scoped plan and ended with `no patch or evidence was submitted` plus the generic `something went wrong: model ended turn without submitting`; the suggested `tm run T-1` retry did not recover in this one-trial run, and tm itself ran no tests. The requested `tm events` command only displayed subcommand help and exited 64, so I had to discover `tm events tail --from 1 --no-follow --json`. A visible Path-focused plan, compact/deduplicated read context, a more diagnostic final failure message that explains what is present and how to resume, and an actionable finite default for event inspection would make tm clearer, cheaper, and more recoverable.

OpenCode stated a concise three-step plan, found src/click/types.py and the typing context quickly, and corrected its initial bounded-TypeVar attempt after a targeted mypy assertion showed Path narrowing incorrectly; its own focused runtime/type checks then passed. The hidden PR test files mechanically failed afterward: the runtime generic-specialization test failed because Path was not runtime-generic, while mypy and pyright reported `Never`/`Unknown` for default Path instances. It should preserve a non-generic/default Path value type when path_type is omitted and make Path subscriptable at runtime, then run the full PR typing file plus focused runtime tests before declaring verification complete.
